chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who lends another man impure dirhams, and takes from him fresh dirhams, which please him. He said: 'There is no problem,' and mentioned that this is from Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to repay a loan of debased coins with fresh, high-quality coins?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* establishes the permissibility of repaying a loan of debased currency with superior quality coins, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the debtor fulfills the obligation by returning the equivalent value or better, rather than the exact physical specimens. The chain of narration linking this ruling to Imam Ali (peace be upon him) underscores its foundational status in early Islamic commercial law, addressing practical economic concerns regarding currency fluctuation and trust (*thiqa*) in transactions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the man who lent Dirhams impure to the man and took the new ones from him with his agreement. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’, and he<sup>asws</sup> mentioned: ‘That is from Ali<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb who has said the following: “

This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who gave impure dirhams as a loan to another man, who then paid him back with better dirhams without compulsion. He (the Imam) said, Tt is not unlawful and it is from Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam.’”
